episodes.163950: A convergent rain band associated with a coastal trough and near record high precipitable water values caused training of cells within Ft. Pierce and Port St. Lucie, prompting localized flash flooding. Rain totals of 6-12 inches occurred, with most of the rain falling in less than 12-hours, and the greatest accumulations happening in less than 6-hours. Many roads were inundated and had to be closed.
episodes.163951: A band of onshore moving showers producing strong wind gusts along the coast near the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant.
episodes.164179: A cold front moved across the state on the 21st bringing scattered showers and thunderstorms including a severe storm that brought hail to portions of Independence and Jackson Counties. Hail was reported to be as large as 1.25 in Diaz and Jacksonport (Jackson County).
episodes.164237: The Minneapolis Shoal Light station on the Bay of Green Bay measured storm force northwest wind gusts on the evening of the 21st.
episodes.164238: Storm force wind gusts were reported over portions of Lake Superior on the 21st in the wake of a cold frontal passage.
episodes.164545: A cold front pushed into the Mid-South on November 21, 2021. A few strong thunderstorms developed over eastern Arkansas during the afternoon producing some small hail.

events.location: 0.61 E St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant
events.narrative: A mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 37 knots near the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant, along the immediate coast of Hutchinson Island as a heavy shower moved onshore.
Nickel size hail covered the ground.

events.county: Manitou Island To Marquette Mi And W Of Grand Marais Mi To Us/Canadian Border Beyond 5Nm Of Shore
events.narrative: The Stannard Rock C-MAN station measured storm force west-northwest winds throughout the period with a peak gust of 68 mph at 308 pm on the 21st.

Extreme rainfall, with totals of 6-12 inches fell in less than 12 hours, with much of the rain occurring in less than 6-hours. Numerous roadways in Port St. Lucie, White City and adjacent Ft. Pierce South experienced rapid inundation, resulting in stalled cars and blocked roads. Numerous roads were closed with water approaching several homes. Water accumulated to heights of 2.5 to 3 feet near Kitterman Road and U.S. Highway 1 (Port St. Lucie) and Gopher Ridge Road (White City). The highest rain measurement was 11.40 inches from a Weather Underground mesonet site located 4 miles north of Port St. Lucie.
